subject: pine marten
title: A Squirrel Hunter Is Helping Red Squirrels Win Back Scotland

scenes.text: Red squirrels are coming back in Scotland, thanks to a predator that hunts squirrels.
Grey squirrels from North America pushed the native reds out with competition and a pox reds can't survive.
Then pine martens, native forest hunters, started returning to Scotland's woods.
From 2014 to 2017, scientists tracked them with hair traps and DNA. Where martens spread, greys dropped away.
Reds grew cautious around martens. Greys didn't, which likely makes them easier prey.
So the red squirrel's best friend is an animal that hunts squirrels.

description:
Red squirrels are recovering in Scotland thanks to a predator that hunts squirrels: the pine marten.
Invasive grey squirrels from North America outcompete native reds for food and carry a pox the reds have no defence against. A 2014 to 2017 study in Scotland (Sheehy, Lambin, Sutherland and colleagues, Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2018) used hair traps and DNA to map returning pine martens and found that marten exposure strongly cut grey squirrel numbers while red squirrels benefited. Reds became more cautious where martens were active; greys showed no such caution, suggesting they are easier prey.
Can a predator be the best thing that happens to its prey?
first_comment: Grey squirrels never met pine martens in North America, and they never learned to be careful. Should Britain let martens spread south?
